steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Head for the surface?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: The Durins have never been to the surface before!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Uh, didn't Stitch? And the people who brought all those library books back from overground?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: And look, nothing in the rulebook says you can't, right?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I mean, listen to you guys. The tunnel's too dangerous, a new shelter's gonna take too long.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So, you head up top and take refuge in Acahualla for a while. That's the best plan to me.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: That lift could hardly hold so many...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I really want to refute you, but...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Your group missed it during your time in Zeruertza, but trains are by far the most common means of transport in Durin society.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Though lifts are convenient for vertical movement...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Durin cities aren't nomadic, so they face the risk of destruction from the moment they're built. Lifts that can only move vertically have far less use to them than trains do.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Moreover, Durin explorers have calculated that Durin cities often lie 1000 to 1500m below the surface. Hardly any cities exist outside of that range.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Which is to say, Durins probe the underground in horizontals. It's rare for there to be one city just a hundred, maybe two hundred meters below another.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Uh... so what does this have to do with the lift?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I know explaining this to you is a waste of time, but I have to show responsibility for others here.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What? All you're trying to tell me is trains are more Durin-handy, yeah?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: *sigh* I suppose so.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And given that, what purpose would a lift then have for existing?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I get it. It's for resources, isn't it?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I don't claim to know why the Durins tend to expand their cities horizontally. Some kind of ingrained habit, I guess.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: But forget that. It doesn't mean they scout out resources horizontally as well. Right?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I thought you were playing the braggart when you claimed you'd been places. I can definitely see your prowess now.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Wowie.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Gavial, check it. Even Miss Avdotya here sees my worth better than you do.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Big whoop. Don't care.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Miss Avdotya, next time you get into an argument with Gavial, I'm on your side.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I'll be fine, thank you.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Anyhow, you're correct. The Durins are filled with a passion for probing underground, especially for minerals.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: In addition, city planning requires the joint decisions of many, while digging is something each Durin is free to commit to at their leisure.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Consequently, they often end up digging several hundred meters above or below their cities out of sheer unawareness.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: In fact, quite a number of Durin historians believe...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: The first Durin lift was only designed when an industrial representative discovered a vein in the roof of their very own city, and that it would be most convenient to dig straight to it.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: However, following an unchecked surge of Durin interest in the surface, such lifts have often been used as shortcuts to the overground.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Huh... so you're saying Durins mainly use it to shift ore, and sometimes there's little scamps like Stitch hitching a ride on them to have some surface fun.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I've told you, I'm about the same age as you, Gavial!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Uh-huh, sure. So, I mean, I get all that, but I still don't understand what you're getting AT.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Miss Avdotya's trying to say that since Durin lifts are mostly designed for industry, they're real sturdy stuff.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Tomimi and me sure noticed that when we came down. The lift could hold a few dozen people, no sweat.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: So, Gavial, your suggestion's pretty feasible.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Right, Master Edge?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Hear, hear.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: I can confirm, the Super Convenient Lift-o-Matic #1 was designed after a vote, which came after some numbskull with nothing to do found a vein up above.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: But then we found a vein even closer, so the thing went by the wayside.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Oh, that tracks. I heard that one cave got mined clean. You think it was you Durin guys who dug the entire cave out in the first place?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: That, I couldn't say. It's possible.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: In addition, to cope with potential future situations, the Durins would have naturally dug out more space while planning the lift, for ease of future enlargement.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Which means, if we're going to make the most reasonable use of our remaining time, enlarging the lifts and getting the Durins to the surface is definitely the way to go.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Oh. You could've just said that then.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: If you only know what to do, and not why you're doing it, then you'll run into setbacks someday.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah, I know that.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But I'm a doctor, Avdotya.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: And look, you know it deep down, don't you?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: How could I ever not trust you?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Why didn't anyone tell me we were getting along so well?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: In my opinion, we're already best buds.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Long and short of it is, I approve of Gavial's suggestion.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: You can hammer out the remaining details. I'll be continuing the survey.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I'll help you out, Master Edge. My Arts can transmit info. If you turn up any results, I can notify everyone first thing.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Aye.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Oh, yeah, I forgot.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Miss Avdotya, I understand. You're against returning to the surface, and your own experiences inform that.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: But you're one of Zeruertza's driving citizens, too. Your opinion swings things.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: And you're an honorable person, on top of that. Now's not the time for it, and you get that, don't you?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Alright, everyone. Rustle us up a happy plan.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: I'll help Master Edge too. No point in tossing around landmark designs now.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Huh? Not like there's anything you can do in there, right?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Can I not be concerned for my own city?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Oh. Sure. Knock yourself out.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So, Avdotya, you still against it?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: (Deep breath in and out)

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: If this is the best method we have to save the people of Zeruertza, then my small contrarianism hardly amounts to anything.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: However. Gavial.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: You're very strong. Stronger, even, than most Ursus soldiers I've met.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: But this isn't a problem you can solve with just strength.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Have you thought about how we're dealing with hundreds of thousands of Durins here?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: If hundreds of thousands of people showed up out of nowhere in a region of Sargon, do you know how terrifying that would be?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: This isn't something you can solve just by telling us your rainforest is big enough.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: How will the region's lord ameer react?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And how will Sargon as a nation react?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: They're going to the surface because they believe in you, but if the reality awaiting them is crueler still...

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Do you still have the courage to say that no other way will work?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Gavial, you would be the most fitting lord ameer for Acahualla. You are the only one who can rein in each and every Tiacauh.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Everyone is awaiting your return.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: And if you simply cannot do it, then it's ultimately likely... that a lord ameer from the Court of Sargon will come to govern Acahualla instead.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: And when that happens, Acahualla will no longer be the free land you knew.
Gavial swallows a sliver of hesitation.
She realizes the choice is now facing her, waiting, and she didn't even notice that it came.
No, she's not unwilling to assume this duty. Far from it.
Not even on her vagrant trails, not even in her days on end at Rhodes Island, did she ever forget Acahualla and her people.
However—
Neither has she forgotten the decision she made, when she resolved to leave Acahualla in the first place.
She was going to study medicine. She was going to save the Oripathy sufferers.
Those two choices she made were the right ones, and they were what she wanted. That's how simple it was. That's why she's never found it this hard to choose.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: So it seems it's crossed your mind. You're not that much a simpleton.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: So, Gavial. If you truly can settle this problem, then I would be willing to even persuade the Durins for you.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: What is your answer?
But. Just as Avdotya says, if this is the only way to save Zeruertza...
If her becoming the lord ameer would solve this problem...
If this is the price she must pay to abide by her own ideals—
Then in that case—

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: I—I'll be Acahualla's lord ameer, and I'll bear the responsibility for this!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Tomimi?!

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Zeruertza's... going to be destroyed?

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Ha, haha... that's a seriously unfunny joke.
Stitch lifts his head, and lifts his gaze to the dome.
He'd been avoiding repairing it all along. Avoiding redesigning the thing, perhaps.
He'd always assumed he'd still have time.
Only now does he realize, he's out. It's gone. He has time no longer.

steps.name: Stitch Canvas
steps.text: Teacher, it seems my hope of surpassing you is behind me.
Stitch jumps aboard a small boat, and sails it for the other shore.
He has to find somewhere to calm down.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Tomimi, what are you doing here?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: We were bringing Master Edge's equipment and workers over, and came to see how it was going while were here.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Looks like we were right to do it.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You two as well... Hold on, so, Tomimi, have you ever actually, seriously, considered what you just said?

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Of course I have!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Acahualla's always been without a lord ameer, Miss Avdotya.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: It's just like you said. If all those Durins went to the surface, they'd draw the attention of the Sargon government for sure.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: So before that happens, I—I'll be the Sargon lord ameer to govern the Acahualla region, and I'll make all of this smooth and simple!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: No lord ameer? Even then, becoming a lord ameer isn't...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I hold the status of Sargon's government-posted Acahuallan Messenger... and scout.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: If I assist, then provided Acahualla comes to have a lord ameer before drawing government attention, this incident can be wholly suppressed.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: That should ease some of your concern, correct?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But, Tomimi, you...

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: It's alright! This way, you don't need to go to any trouble, Gavial!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I mean, yeah, but...

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: No pressure, Gavial.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Tomimi's volunteering to do it, and if she doesn't, then I can do it too.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Mm-hm!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Zumama...

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Or are you scared? You think you made a mistake?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I don't, I just have this weird feeling...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Let me think up a way to describe it.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah. Okay, it's like. I've got this giant boulder in front of me right now.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: And I'm thinking, I have to use up so much of my strength just to break it.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But once I give it a shot, something tells me, wow, you can break this thing so easily.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: But it's like, why? Even though it's so big.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Gavial, how's the axe I made you? Handy?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah. Honestly, even more handy than I thought. I like it a lot.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I stayed for days straight making it for you, and the materials are all the best I could get too.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What? C'mon, you should've said so sooner. I'm embarrassing myself here.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I'm telling you because I want you to understand—I don't need you to thank me for making these things for you.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Because—

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Because Gavial's Gavial!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: What the hell does that mean?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Something very simple—

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Your fists are bigger than you think, Gavial.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Because you have me.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: And me!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: And the Rhodes Islanders, and all the people you've saved, and everyone in Acahualla too.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Because in the end, you're right, Gavial.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Ultimately, all those guys you beat into submission are willing to recognize you, because they realize that in the end, you're right.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Gavial, you believe in the right things. You've never gone wrong.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: We all believe in you, Gavial.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: So, our fists are your fists.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: And you can keep on believing in your fists.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: All you've gotta do is charge ahead, Gavial! We'll help you out!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You guys...

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Oh, but, but—

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Zumama, next time you make equipment for Gavial, I want to help too!

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I can do it myself.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: No, it's unfair only having a Zumama charm! I want to draw on my... my dreamcatcher! And the 'Gavial's Will' mark! And, and...

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Uh, no can do, Tomimi, that's too much.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: *wail* I'll only draw three!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: If you don't let me draw anything, your tail will turn thick!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: No putting curses on my tail!

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: *whimper* Gavial, please don't bonk my head...
Standing by Avdotya, Inam can sense that this Lupo woman to her side is having a somewhat hard time believing her eyes.
But to herself, it's a trivial, banal thing.
She lets out a small sigh.
She knows that finally, she's come to a decision too.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: And on that note, I have a better proposal.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Inam?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I'll serve as Acahualla's lord ameer.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I've hung around with you as a government Messenger for all these years. I have the right to stand for lord ameer.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I just didn't want to before, that's all.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Seeing as we'd have to force Tomimi back from Rhodes Island, whereas I've been in Acahualla the whole time, I'd make a tidier fit for lord ameer, wouldn't I?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: And I imagine that better assuages your concerns, Avdotya.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Yes, it does, but I have to say, you people really boggle my mind...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: They're... no, we're just a couple of fools living in the rainforest.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Inam, are you really sure about this?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Well, this way, you won't need to leave Gavial, will you?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Gavial, I have this feeling we'll be fine friends, won't we?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Hahaha, of course we will!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: If you insist, then hell, go right on ahead!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Now I see. All else aside, you've definitely persuaded me. I'll make good on my commitment.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: However, Gavial, don't get carried away yet.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: An entire city's worth of people are headed for the surface. There's no precedent for something like this in all of Durin history.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: It's something the entire city has to decide on, and if the people ultimately dissent, then we're out of luck.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Which is exactly why we need you to talk 'em over.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Not a worry. I made you my promise. I'll do all I can.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Haha. Thanks.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: (Under breath) Honestly, I should be thanking you on behalf of all of Zeruertza.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Huh? What did you say?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I said, I need to return and make some preparations.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Alright, I'll—

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Are you able to draft my speech for me?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Yeah, no.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Then I suggest you do something that plays to your strengths. If I do need your help at any point, I'll let you know.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Gotcha.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Alright, Inam, we've gotta get you and Zumama back to the surface stat. Evac the elderly and children to someplace around Acahualla.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Next—

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Taskforce with the working adults to enlarge the lifts, right?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You got it.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: No problem.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: What about me, Gavial?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You stay by my side, Tomimi.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Avdotya's good on assistance, so let's go see if we can help Master Edge out with anything.

steps.name: Tomimi
steps.text: Mm-hm!

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Alright, 'scuse us.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Come to think of it... Zumama.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I know this isn't too realistic, but... I'm supposing we can't return the way you and Gavial originally came?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Yep, that's not quite happening.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Then we'll need someone to show the way. The cave network's considerably complex above the network. I haven't forgotten as much for a single second.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Stitch could work, since he brought us down. Elysium too; he might even find the way better than Stitch did.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: No need. Seeing as we still have time, you come with me.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I'll be honest; luck played an enormous part in Stitch emerging from such a complex network alive.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And Elysium's helping Master Edge out, so let's let him be here.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You mean to say you know the way?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: The likelihood is, nobody in modern-day Zeruertza does.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: But you know the Durin adventurers, filled with the spirit of exploration? Each time they finish a foray, they're always happy to record everything they've seen and heard in books, so they can share with their companions.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And in the library, I once read such an adventurer's log, which finely detailed how he went through the cave network above the lift, and made it to the surface.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: And while I don't know where said adventurer is now, he was considerate enough to leave behind a map.
